findings.title: Vector3.rotateAroundAxis() is not an isometry when the axis normalizes to zero: it returns v*cos(angle)
findings.expected: A rotation of v by any axis the method can normalize is length preserving; for a zero axis the natural fallback (used by every other zero-normal guard in the repo) is the identity, i.e. the input vector.
findings.actual: axis.clone().normalize() leaves the zero axis at (0,0,0); the Rodrigues terms dot=0 and cross=0, so the result is v*cos(angle).
findings.tolerance: 1e-12 absolute per component, 1e-12 relative for the length
findings.why_a_bug: A rotation matrix must satisfy |R v| = |v|. The method performs its own axis normalization, so it advertises support for arbitrary nonzero axis vectors, yet the zero axis silently produces a scaled vector instead of a rotation, an exception, or a warning. The failure is 100% of the vector magnitude, not floating-point noise.
findings.strongest_alternative_explanation: No live call site in src/: cable_joints_core.js:485 _rotateAroundAxis is unused and its axis comes from a plane normal guarded against zero, so no current simulation result depends on this. The only callers anywhere are archived research prototypes under output/research/sessions/2026-10-20-interactive-research-62300644/*-core.mjs (also passing guarded plane normals). That makes F1 latent, but it remains a genuine defect of a public helper any new caller can hit.
findings.reachability: No live caller. `grep -rn rotateAroundAxis src hp-sim-3d tests` finds only the definition; cable_joints_core.js:485 _rotateAroundAxis is unused. Archived prototypes under output/research/sessions/ call it.

findings.title: Quaternion.normalize() returns the zero quaternion and Vector3.normalize() returns NaN outside the representable length range
findings.status: genuine, latent (no plausible call site reaches the range)
findings.expected: normalize() returns a unit vector for every finite nonzero input (the only documented/implemented special case is length 0, which returns the identity quaternion).
findings.actual: lengthSq overflows to Infinity for any component >= ~1e154, so l = 1/Infinity = 0 and every component becomes 0. For vectors whose length is subnormal (<= ~2.2e-308), 1/l overflows to Infinity and the components become Infinity/NaN.
findings.why_a_bug: normalize() silently returns a value that is not a rotation (the zero quaternion) or not a number, instead of a unit value or an error. The defect is fixable with a plain two-step rescale (divide by max|component| before squaring), so it is not an inherent limit of doubles.
findings.strongest_alternative_explanation: All quaternions in the simulation are built from products of unit quaternions and renormalized, so |q| stays within a few ulp of 1 and the failing band is unreachable in practice; the underflow case needs a vector of length 1e-310, which no position in the scene is. This is why the finding is reported as latent, and no simulation result is affected.
findings.reachability: No reachable path found: setFromAxisAngle's axis argument is documented as normalized and every call site passes a normalized axis; all quaternion products stay unit length.

limitations.title: _tangentPointCircle silently returns a radial (non-tangent) point when the attach point projects inside the guide circle
limitations.measurement: For p at 0.999, 0.9, 0.5, 0.0 radii from the centre and r=1: |T-C| = 1, |cos(radius, span)| = 1.000000 in every case (0 would be a true tangent). In 3D, a point 3.041 m from the centre whose in-plane projection is 0.5 m gives |cos| = 1.000000.
limitations.classification: Documented-by-code graceful fallback for geometrically impossible input (no tangent exists). It is the branch that makes the tangent fuzz skip ~343/4000 random cases.
limitations.not_a_defect_because: No tangent line exists for an interior point; the branch returns the nearest circle point and keeps the result finite and on the circle. Callers that need a tangent must ensure the projection is outside the guide.

limitations.title: symmetric pseudo-inverse loses the M P M = M identity in a narrow band of near-singular tensors
limitations.measurement: I_min/I_max = 1e-16 or below: rel |MPM-M| ~ 9e-16, max|P| = 1 (direction correctly dropped). 1e-15: 1.18e-1, max|P| ~ 1e15. 1e-13: 1.07e-3. 1e-10: 8.6e-7. 1e-6: 8.1e-11.
limitations.classification: Conditioning, not an implementation error. The threshold Number.EPSILON*3*max|diag| sits at the FP noise level of the eigendecomposition, so directions within ~1e-15 of the largest eigenvalue are numerically indistinguishable from zero and get inverted.
limitations.not_a_defect_because: Exactly singular tensors (zero eigenvalue authored) round-trip to 7.8e-16, and ratios down to 1e-6 (a 1 m rod of 1 mm radius) keep the inverse accurate to 1e-10. No shipped body has a smaller principal-moment ratio (all shipped physics:inertiaTensor values are isotropic diagonals).

limitations.title: Vector3.angleTo has an acos resolution floor near 1e-8 rad
limitations.classification: Standard acos conditioning; 1e-8 rad = 2 nanodegrees. Not a defect for any scene tolerance (0.5 deg).

limitations.title: cable_shape's parabolic fallback loses all slack for near-vertical spans (horizontal span <= 1e-5 m)
limitations.classification: Documented approximation in the module header ('a parabolic approximation when nearly vertical'); the fallback sags along upDirection, which is degenerate when the span is vertical.
limitations.not_a_defect_because: The trigger needs a horizontal span <= 10 um. All shipped cable spans are >= ~20 mm, and the near-taut catenary branch (the realistic case) reproduces the rest length to 4.7e-14 by independent numerical integration.

limitations.title: signedArcLengthOnWheel cannot represent a wrap of 2*pi or more
limitations.measurement: sweep 2*pi+0.3 and 4*pi+0.3 both return 0.3 rad; a 3*pi/2 sweep returns -1.571 signed / 4.712 force-positive (the cw arc).
limitations.classification: Model limitation: the wrap is inferred from two attachment points only, so it is defined modulo 2*pi. It returns the preferred-direction arc in [0, 2*pi), which is the only information available.
limitations.not_a_defect_because: No pair of attachment points can determine a multi-turn wrap; callers that know the wrap keep it in the authored cablePath:stored.

limitations.title: normalizeInertiaTensor does not validate physical admissibility (triangle inequality, symmetry, positive definiteness)
limitations.measurement: An authored diag(1,1,10) (I3 > I1+I2, physically impossible for a real body) is passed through verbatim and used as the inverse inertia.
limitations.classification: Deliberate coercion ('normalize' means shape/type coercion here, with finite fallbacks) rather than sanitisation.
limitations.not_a_defect_because: All shipped physics:inertiaTensor values are isotropic diagonal tensors, and composites built from them by parallels-axis addition automatically satisfy the triangle inequality (verified over 3000 random point-mass bodies).

limitations.title: Attempted audit of baked attachment points in shipped scenes was inconclusive
limitations.measurement: Reconstructing each rolling body's centre from xformOp:translate gave |P-C|/r errors up to 13% on hp4/hp5_pulley_reduced, which we traced to pinhole_gate steps where link index i is not bounded by jointResults[i].body0Path.
limitations.classification: Method limitation, so no numbers from that audit are used in this report.

limitations.title: Degenerate zero-length / zero-mass / duplicate-point inputs are handled without NaN
limitations.measurement: closestPointOnSegment(p,a,a) = a; parallelAxisTensor(0, offset) = 0; MomentOfInertiaComponent(0).inertia = 0; slack cable with start==end stays finite and starts/ends exactly on the endpoints; segments=0 returns only the end point (no NaN).

unresolved: Whether the degenerate (interior-projection) tangent branch is reachable in any shipped scene: our body-centre reconstruction was not reliable across pinhole_gate links.
The 2-5e-5 tangency residual we measured for layered (halfWidth > 0) baked attachments is consistent with the hybrid knot radius from storedToRadiusAndTheta, but we did not isolate it.
Multi-turn (> 2*pi) guide wraps: not representable by the two-attachment-point model; we did not check whether any real HP4/HP5 wrap needs it.

prior_work_not_duplicated.reused: That session already reported the USD xformOpOrder/translation defect (F1), the metersPerUnit defect (F3), and the !invert!/xformOp:scale observation. This session does not re-report them; it only verifies that the rotate*ABC quaternion conversion itself matches pxr.
